title: AI-Augmented Software Development
syllabus: Introduction to LLM-based software engineering: Role of LLMs in the software development lifecycle - coding assistants - testing and debugging support - documentation and review - limitations of LLM outputs - academic integrity and responsible use. Prompting as interface design: Role and task specification - constraints and acceptance criteria - input/output formatting - structured prompting - prompt refinement for software tasks - prompt reuse as configuration artifact. LLMs as software components: LLM APIs - request/response patterns - context handling - conversation state - output parsing - schema-based validation - error handling and retries. Structured outputs and integration: JSON outputs - lightweight schemas - deterministic wrappers - validation before execution - integration into software pipelines. From assistants to agents: Chatbots versus agents - perceive-think- act-observe loop - tool use - simple state handling - single-agent task execution. Tools and tool registries: Function/tool calling - tool abstraction - file, search, and execution tools - schemas for tools - permissions and scope control. Agent harness engineering: Harness definition - bounded execution - step limits - runtime policies - trace logging - human-in-the-loop approvals - failure handling and recovery. Agentic workflow patterns: ReAct-style loops - planner-executor pattern - retrieval-assisted workflows - choosing the simplest effective orchestration pattern. Evaluation harnesses: Task suites - success criteria - regression testing - step count, latency, and error metrics - qualitative evaluation - LLM-as-judge and rubric-based assessment. Observability and debugging: Trajectories and traces - prompt/tool/output inspection - episode logging - failure attribution - improving prompts, tools, and harness settings from evidence. Safety and governance: Prompt injection overview - unsafe tool use - privacy and data leakage risks - permission design - sandboxing - human review for high -impact actions. Capstone development and review: Team project planning - design of an LLM-integrated or agentic system - implementation with runtime harness and evaluation harness - demo and technical reflection.
source_locator: Courses of Study (Oct 2026), Course Contents PDF p.86; category/semester: Courses of Study (Oct 2026), BTech DSAI curriculum tables + semester plan (printed p.24-25)

title: Reinforcement Learning
syllabus: Module 1 RL Foundations & Dynamic Programming - Theory: Agent-environment-reward framework, Markov Decision Processes: returns, value functions and Bellman equations: policy evaluation, policy improvement, policy iteration and value iteration. Lab: Build a GridWorld/FrozenLake MDP; implement policy iteration and value iteration; visualise value functions and optimal policy. Module 2 Monte Carlo & Temporal Difference Methods - Theory: Monte Carlo prediction and control- on-policy vs off-policy learning (brief importance sampling): TD(O), SARSA, Q-learning. Lab: Tabular MC control, SARSA and Q-learning on FrozenLake/Taxi/CliffWalking; compare on-policy vs off-policy behaviour. Module 3 DeepRL: Value-Based & Policy-Gradient Foundations - Theory: Function approximation, neural-network value functions: Deep Q -Networks: experience replay and target networks, policy - gradient theorem - REINFORCE. Lab: DQN on CartPole to LunarLander (replay buffer + target net); REINFORCE on CartPole. Module 4 Actor-Critic & Advanced Deep RL - Theory: Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C): deterministic policy gradients and DDPG - TD3 - Soft Actor-Critic and entropy regularization, exploration strategies ( ε- greedy, entropy-based). Lah: A2C on a discrete task; SAC or TD3 on Pendulum I continuous control (Stable-Baselines3). Module 5 Model-Based, Multi-Agent, Exploration & Safe RL - Theory: Environment-dynamics modeling and planning (Dyna-Q) - cooperative vs competitive MARL: MADDPG and QMIX (overview) - curiosity- driven exploration - meta-RL and transfer (brief) - safe/constrained RL. Lab: Dyna-Q planning; one multi-agent or curiosity-driven task (PettingZoo or exploration-bonus agent). Module 6 Advanced RL: PPO, DPO & RLHF - Theory: Trust regions and Proximal Policy Optimization - preference-based RL -Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: reward modeling and the RLHF pipeline- Direct Preference Optimization - alignment of large models. Lab: PPO (from scratch or SB3) on LunarLander/custom env; mini RLHF/DPO pipeline on a small language model using HuggingFace TRL with a tiny preference dataset.
prerequisite_text: Either CSL304 or CS550/DSL501 and MAL403 or equivalent
